newsitem.title: CANADA: Int'l Panorama says Congo ratifies project.
newsitem.headline: Int'l Panorama says Congo ratifies project.

text.p: International Panorama Resource Corp said on Wednesday its Kakanda/Kambove copper and cobalt project in the former Zaire was formally ratified by the new mines minister for the Democratic Republic of Congo.
A recent prefeasibility study projected production of 3,500 tonnes of cobalt and 45,000 tonnes of copper a year for more than 15 years.
International Panorama said it was proceeding with a full feasibility study and expected to begin production in mid-1999. Capital expenditures are estimated at US$240 million.
Until that investment is repaid, 85 percent of revenues will be used to repay capital expenditures and 15 percent paid to the joint venture partners.
After payback, the company would receive 51 percent of revenues and state-owned Gecamines 49 percent.
International Panorama said it expected revenues for its 51 percent interest in the project to exceed US$664 million, after capital payback and a royalty of 1.5 percent to Gecamines.

"This would result in average annual earnings...in excess of US$41 million. The prefeasibility study suggests a net present value of US$203 million and an internal rate of return of 47 percent for International Panorama's interest in the project," the company said.
